$comment: THE machine-readable Flash plugin protocol contract — the single source of truth for version, deadlines, quotas, error strings, the capability registry and transport limits. Normativity order: this file > docs/plugin-protocol.md prose > any implementation. Swift asserts its constants equal this file (PluginProtocolParityTests); the Rust SDK asserts its transport limits against it (wire.rs) and pins the behaviour in its runtime tests and probe crate. Changing anything here is a protocol change: update the host, SDK, affected plugins, tests, and docs in the same commit (repo rule 7 — no compatibility shims, no version bump while Flash has no external users).

deadlines_ms.$comment: One deadline table. startup: initialize must be answered immediately (no warm-catalog wait; config [plugins] startup_timeout tunes it). query: per-keystroke evaluate. hints: activation hint pull; the activation waits on it ahead of the prepared model, so it is a fixed latency ceiling, while the AX queue serves other walks; a screen-scope walk and a commit revalidating its target wait on their queue for the same reply. text_grid: the letter-search grid pull, asked asynchronously only when the focused app publishes no Accessibility text; the search waits on it, so it shares the hints ceiling. search: the live flashlight pull of a query scoped to a live source; the flashlight drops the reply to a query the user has typed past, so a late one costs nothing but its rows. perform: all three kinds. ping: reply budget for the idle-liveness probe (sent only after idle_before_ping_ms of inbound silence with no request in flight; ONE miss tears down). shutdown_grace: stdin-close -> SIGTERM; +500ms -> SIGKILL.

host_to_plugin.initialize: request {protocol_version} -> {ok, protocol_version}; reply immediately, once ever; ok:false or a version mismatch is terminal (flush, exit 0)
host_to_plugin.event: notification {name, payload}; never replied; `core:poll:<name>` ticks a cadence registered through `poll` and bypasses `listen`; `core:status.observed` carries {segments: [name]}, the complete set of unique nonempty manifest `status` names of this plugin that a status surface shows (empty = none), sent once after initialize and again on every change
host_to_plugin.evaluate: request {query} -> {ok, answers}; CPU-only over pre-warmed state
host_to_plugin.hints: request {bundle_id, pid, front_window_frame, display_scale? (physical pixels per AppKit point)} -> {ok, targets, context_pid?}; always live
host_to_plugin.text_grid: request {bundle_id, pid, front_window_frame, display_scale? (physical pixels per AppKit point)} -> {ok, columns, rows, lines, cell?}; always live; sent to the focused app's hint providers in hint order, first non-empty grid wins; each line is one text_grid_line shape; cell is the text_grid_cell shape, and without it the host divides the window evenly by columns and rows; empty lines = no grid
host_to_plugin.search: request {source, query} -> {ok, rows}; always live; source is a manifest sources[].name that declares `live`, query the text typed after the scope (always empty for a per_scope source); each row is one row shape carrying that source, the reply under quotas.catalog_rows and quotas.catalog_bytes; a malformed or over-quota reply is served as no rows, and the rows never enter the catalog
host_to_plugin.perform: request {kind: resolve|command|navigate, ...} -> {ok, target_pid?, navigation_url?, message?, alert?} | {ok:false, unhandled:true} | {ok:false, error}; a command is one perform_command shape: a core command the manifest declares under one of Flash's topics (with context), the plugin's own command or a bang (without); a resolve is {row, confirmed?}; confirmed is the `confirmation` section's; alert is one perform_alert shape

plugin_to_host_notifications.publish: {rows, source?} — the plugin's catalog, host-owned store. Without `source`: a full replacement of every source's rows. With `source` (a manifest sources[].name that every row carries): a replacement of that source's rows alone, the other sources keeping theirs — a publish stays proportional to the change when volatile and static rows are separate sources. Quotas apply to the whole catalog after the merge; empty rows = authoritative empty (of the catalog, or of that source); transient failure = don't publish (host keeps last-good). The host decodes publishes on a queue that carries no replies, so a publish and a later reply are not ordered host-side; publishes of one plugin keep their order.
plugin_to_host_notifications.status: {segments: {name: value}} — manifest-declared names only; value is markup ("" clears) or a carousel object {prefix?: markup, lines: [markup], cycle_seconds: >= 1} the host rotates on its own clock (no lines clears; malformed objects are rejected whole)
plugin_to_host_notifications.poll: {registrations: {name: {every: seconds, priority} | {after: seconds, priority}}} — full-replacement set of the cadences (`every`) and one-shot deadlines (`after`, measured from receipt) the host should drive for this plugin; empty clears. Plugins must not arm their own timers or sleep to schedule work: the host folds every registration in the app onto one clock and sends `event {name: "core:poll:<name>"}` when one is due, regardless of manifest `listen`. A deadline fires once; repeating it unchanged in a later set neither re-arms nor re-fires it, and a changed or new name arms it afresh. Ticks are one-way and unacknowledged, so a plugin still running its previous callback drops the ones it missed instead of catching up. Bounds live in the `poll` section; a malformed or over-bound frame is rejected whole.
plugin_to_host_notifications.log: {level, message, fields, trace?} — content-free; trace names the interaction of the request being served

host_events.$comment: Every `core:*` event the host delivers through `event`, gated by manifest `listen`. `replacement` kinds are state signals: each supersedes the earlier ones with the same coalescing key, the event name plus, for core:ax.changed, the payload pid and notification. While a replacement frame waits unsent in the host's outbound queue, a newer one with the same key drops it and joins the tail, so a child reads a subsequence of the emitted events in emission order; requests, responses and other events stay FIFO under the transport budget. Under backlog the plugin likewise keeps only the latest of each key. core:apps.changed (payload {running_applications: [{bundle_id, pid, localized_name}]}) carries the complete snapshot of running regular apps. core:window.focus.changed (payload {pid, bundle_id}) names the app whose focused or main window changed. core:ax.changed (payload {pid, notification, bundle_id?}; both pid and a non-empty notification are required) reports one AX notification an observed app posted, one of `ax_notifications`: the value change of each keystroke is AXValueChanged, so match the notification instead of debouncing every change alike. core:network.changed (network interfaces, addresses, routes or DNS changed; payload {}) and core:volumes.changed (a volume mounted, unmounted or was renamed; payload {}) are payload-free, coalesced signals whose monitors run only while a plugin listens: re-read what you need. core:calendar.changed (payload {}) is the same kind of signal for the calendar database, and for the user answering macOS's Calendars prompt; it reaches only a plugin that holds the calendar_events capability, never an event monitor or a socket client, and the host observes the database only while such a plugin listens and macOS has granted Flash access. core:system.slept and core:system.woke bracket a system sleep, core:displays.slept and core:displays.woke a display sleep, core:screen.locked and core:screen.unlocked the lock screen; all payload {}. core:displays.changed (payload {added: [name], removed: [name], displays: [name]}) reports a display connected or removed. core:space.changed (payload {}) follows the active Space. core:user.idle (payload {seconds}) reports that nobody touched the keyboard, mouse or trackpad for one of the subscribers' idle thresholds (300 s for a plugin), once per away episode and threshold; core:user.active (payload {idle_seconds}) follows when input comes back after an announced episode. core:usb.attached and core:usb.detached (payload {vendor_id?, product_id?, name?}, never a serial number) report a USB device connected or removed; devices already connected are not announced. core:clock.minute (payload {time: "HH:MM", weekday: "mon"…"sun", date: "YYYY-MM-DD", late_seconds}, in the local time zone) reports that a wall-clock minute began; a plugin listener hears every minute. After a sleep or a locked screen it hears only the current minute, with how late it is. core:workspace.changed (payload {workspace, previous?, workspaces: [name]}) follows the focused tiling workspace while [tiling] is on. core:mode.changed (payload {mode, previous, layer?}: normal, insert, command, terminal, hyper, hold, visual, layer or disabled; layer names the active layer) follows Flash's mode. core:hints.shown (payload {surface, targets}) reports a hint session's first labels on screen, core:hints.committed (payload {surface}) each target it commits and core:hints.cancelled (payload {surface}) a session that ended without committing; never which target, its text or its label. core:monitor.triggered (payload {monitor, level: warning|error}) reports a value monitor rising into warning or error; never the value. Every event but core:apps.changed, core:ax.changed, core:calendar.changed, core:session.opened and core:status.observed, the plugin plumbing, also reaches the clients of the resident's socket that subscribe to it (docs/ipc-protocol.md).

poll.$comment: Bounds of a `poll` registration set. priority sets the slack the shared clock may add to a wake-up so unrelated ones coalesce (high 25 ms: a value on screen the user watches change; normal 100 ms: ordinary sampling and settles; low 1 s: background upkeep, remote pulls, retries). The core-only `system` priority is not available to plugins. every is floored at min_every_ms; every and after are capped at max_seconds; a set holds at most max_registrations names of 1..max_name_bytes characters from [a-z0-9_-].

audio_devices.$comment: host.audio_devices: CoreAudio stays in the host. Requests carry operation and exactly the fields it takes; any other key refuses the call. list {direction} -> {ok, devices: [{uid, name, default}]}, sorted by name, default marking the direction's default device. select {direction, uid} -> {ok} makes the device whose UID is uid the default. step_volume {ticks} -> {ok, percent} moves the default output that many macOS volume-key ticks (a sixteenth each, up when positive, down when negative, never zero, at most max_ticks either way), clears its mute and answers the percent the bezel would show. toggle_mute {} -> {ok, muted} mutes or unmutes the default output. volume {} -> {ok, percent, muted} reads it. percent is 0 to 100. A CoreAudio failure answers {ok:false, error}.

system_actions.$comment: host.system_action: the machine and session actions stay in the host. A request carries exactly {action}; any other key refuses the call. It answers {ok:true} once the host asked macOS for the action, or {ok:false, error} with why it could not. lock_screen posts macOS's Lock Screen shortcut to the session; sleep and display_sleep ask IOKit power management; screensaver opens ScreenSaverEngine; toggle_appearance switches dark mode through System Events. The `destructive` actions cannot be undone: restart, shutdown and logout go through System Events, empty_trash through Finder. The host honours a destructive action only inside a perform the user confirmed (see `confirmation`), one action per confirmed perform; outside one it does nothing and answers errors.confirmation_required. The Apple Events are the host's own fixed scripts: the plugin needs no apple_events capability and no target list, its sandbox gains no allowance, and macOS attributes the Automation request to Flash.

process_signals.$comment: host.process_signal: kill(2) stays in the host. A request carries exactly {pid, signal}; any other key refuses the call. pid is an integer of at least min_pid: 0 (the caller's process group), a negative pid (a group, or every process) and 1 (launchd) are refused when the request is decoded, and the host refuses its own pid. term is SIGTERM. The host honours every signal only inside a perform the user confirmed (see `confirmation`), one signal per confirmed perform; outside one it asks the kernel nothing and answers errors.confirmation_required. It answers {ok:true} once the kernel took the signal, or {ok:false, error} with the kernel's reason (No such process, Operation not permitted) or the refusal. The plugin's sandbox gains no allowance.

calendar_events.$comment: host.calendar_events: EventKit and the Calendars grant stay in the host, and macOS names Flash in its prompt. Requests carry operation and exactly the fields it takes; any other key refuses the call. Every success carries `access`, what macOS answers without asking: granted, denied (refused, restricted or write-only) or undetermined (Flash never asked). access {} -> {ok, access} reads it. request_access {} -> {ok, access} reads it too, and when it is undetermined asks macOS first and answers once the user did (granted or denied). The host asks only while the user is using the plugin, that is while one of its performs or searches is in flight or a status surface shows one of its segments; an undetermined access asked about anywhere else answers errors.user_request_required and shows no prompt. Requests made while the prompt is open share its answer, and once the user answered the host sends core:calendar.changed, so a caller that stopped waiting still hears of it. list {start, end, calendars?} -> {ok, access, events?, truncated?} reads the occurrences overlapping start..<end, both Unix seconds from 0 to max_time, start < end, the window at most max_window_seconds long; calendars is at most max_calendars calendar titles as Calendar shows them, each non-empty and at most quotas.title_bytes, and absent or empty reads every event calendar. It never asks: without the grant it answers the access alone, with no events key. events are in start order (then end, then id), each one calendar_event shape. The reply holds at most max_events events and at most reply_bytes of them, counted from their compact encoding; later events are left out and `truncated` is true, and is absent otherwise. An EventKit failure answers {ok:false, error}.

calendar_event.$comment: One occurrence of a host.calendar_events list reply. id is the event's identifier and this occurrence's start (a repeating event's occurrences share the identifier); start and end are Unix seconds; calendar is the title of the calendar it belongs to; declined says the user is an attendee who declined it; canceled is the event's own status. title and calendar are cut at a character boundary to quotas.title_bytes. url is the event's URL field and location its location, each present only when the event has one of at most quotas.url_bytes. The event's notes never cross the wire: links holds the link-shaped runs found in them, in order, each a URL scheme, `:/` and the characters up to the next whitespace, quote or bracket, at most max_links of them and each at most quotas.url_bytes; the key is absent when there is none. Which of these is a meeting link is the plugin's to decide.

app_items.$comment: host.notes, host.reminders and host.contacts (`methods`), each behind the capability of its own name: the items of an Apple app whose grant Flash holds (Automation of Notes, Reminders, Contacts), read by the host; macOS names Flash in its prompt and the plugin's sandbox gains nothing. The three take the same requests. Requests carry operation and exactly the fields it takes; any other key refuses the call. Every success but a show carries `access`, what macOS answers without asking: granted, denied or undetermined (Flash never asked; Notes also reads so while it is not running, since macOS has nobody to ask about). access {} -> {ok, access} reads it. request_access {} -> {ok, access} reads it too, and when it is undetermined and can be asked (Notes: only while Notes runs) asks macOS first and answers once the user did (granted or denied). The host asks only while the user is using the plugin, that is while one of its performs or searches is in flight or a status surface shows one of its segments; an undetermined access asked about anywhere else answers errors.user_request_required and shows no prompt. Requests made while the prompt is open share its answer. list {} -> {ok, access, items?, truncated?} reads every item in the app's own order: every note of every account, every open reminder of every list, every contact card. It never asks: without the grant it answers the access alone, with no items key, and Notes is never launched to answer. Each item is one app_item shape. The reply holds at most max_items items and at most reply_bytes of them, counted from their compact encoding; later items are left out and `truncated` is true, and is absent otherwise. show {id} -> {ok} brings the app forward on the item whose identifier a list returned: id is 1 to max_id_bytes bytes without control characters. It answers {ok:false, error} without the grant, and never asks. Notes is read and shown through the host's own fixed AppleScript, with the id as an escaped literal: no script, terminology or source is accepted from a plugin. A failure of the app, its framework or its script answers {ok:false, error}.

app_item.$comment: One item of a host.notes, host.reminders or host.contacts list reply. id selects the item in its app again (show). title is a note's name, a reminder's title or the name Contacts shows a card by (the person's full name, or a company card's company), cut at a character boundary to quotas.title_bytes; it may be empty. A reminder also carries list, the title of its list (cut the same way), list_index, that list's position among Reminders' lists from 0 (absent when Reminders no longer names the list), and created, the Unix seconds it was created at (absent when it has none); a note and a contact carry none of the three. Nothing else of an item crosses the wire: no note text, no reminder notes or dates due, no phone number, address or other field of a card. Which rows these make, and in what order, is the plugin's to decide.

ax_snapshot.$comment: host.ax_snapshot: Accessibility stays in the host. `root` says which tree one snapshot walks; absent, it is the first of `roots`. windows walks the windows of the app `pid` names (required). menu_bar walks the menu bar of the app that owns it, which the host names: a `pid` beside it refuses the call, and the reply carries that app's `pid` beside `nodes`. Its one root is the app's AXMenuBar, so the first node is the bar, its children the bar items in bar order, the Apple menu first. The host never walks its own process: with no owner but Flash the reply is {ok:true, nodes: []} and carries no pid, as when no app owns the bar. Both roots are one breadth-first walk bounded by max_nodes (default_max_nodes when absent), each element read once for `collect` and `follow` together, within timeout_ms including queue admission; a snapshot that fails returns no node and leaves no handle. A snapshot supersedes the plugin's earlier handles for that app, and a menu_bar one its earlier menu_bar handles for every app, since one app owns the bar at a time. The two roots run on separate host queues, and a call on a handle runs on the queue of the snapshot that returned it, so a menu bar never waits on a window walk.

applescript.$comment: Typed host-owned AppleScript templates; no source code, script field, raw terminology or evaluated strings are accepted. Requests carry operation, timeout_ms and the operation-specific data fields. All strings enter templates only as escaped literals. Supported browser IDs use fixed Chromium/Safari dialects. Every operation checks its actual target against manifest apple_events_targets; shortcuts use com.apple.shortcuts.events, chat_submit uses com.apple.systemevents and now_playing uses the bundle_id it names. now_playing {bundle_id, artist} asks one media player (an app whose scripting has player state and current track) what it plays, never launching it: the result is the player state, a line feed and the current track's name, with its artist after an em dash when artist is true; an app that is not running answers an empty result. The plugin needs apple_events. script_bytes bounds generated source; result_bytes bounds the UTF-8 result; deadlines and per-plugin concurrency include queue admission. The host returns {ok:true,result} or {ok:false,error,status?}; source/results never enter diagnostics.

publish.$comment: The publish notification's params: `rows` always; `source` names the one manifest sources[].name whose rows these replace (every row must carry it), absent for a whole-catalog replacement. Any other key rejects the publish whole.

perform_command.$comment: The perform {kind: command} shape. command and subcommand are the two words (a bang: the plugin id and the token); args are the argument words as a mapping writes them (--index=3, --force, or a bang's query words). context is the focused app and is present exactly for a core command the manifest's commands[] declares under one of Flash's topics, never for a plugin's own command or a bang. count is the NORMAL count typed before the key of the plugin's own command (5 then the key is one perform with count 5), an integer from 1 to count_max; absent means 1, and the host leaves it out for 1, for a core command (which it repeats itself) and for a bang. confirmed is `true` on a command the user confirmed (see `confirmation`), and absent otherwise.

confirmation.$comment: Confirmed destructive actions. A manifest commands[] entry and a row may carry `confirm`: a non-blank question of at most quotas.confirm_bytes. The host asks it through its one confirmation alert before it dispatches that command's perform, or before it acts on that row (its resolve, or its effect), from a key, the command line and the CLI alike, and sends nothing unless the user answers y; a plugin never asks itself. On an own commands[] entry it gates that one pair (never the `*` wildcard); on a core command the plugin performs it gates the command in the apps the plugin's selector matches. A perform sent after the user answered y, to a declared `confirm` or to an `alert confirm` wrapping the command, carries `confirmed: true`; the key is absent otherwise and never false, and a navigate never carries it. The host remembers a confirmed perform until its reply or its deadline, and a host action that needs the user's consent is honoured only while one is in flight for that plugin: each confirmed perform covers one such action.

perform_alert.$comment: The alert a perform reply may carry: the host's centred alert, shown wherever the plugin's own command or bang ran (a key, the CLI, the command line). title alone is a one-line message; title over value is a state (volume over 38%), value one line (no line feed, carriage return, vertical tab, form feed, U+0085, U+2028 or U+2029); widest_value, the widest value the alert shows (100%), keeps its box one size while the value changes and comes only with a value. Every string is non-blank; title is at most quotas.alert_title_bytes, value and widest_value at most quotas.alert_value_bytes. A malformed alert rejects the whole reply. With an alert, message is the caller's output alone: the CLI prints it, the command line shows it, and a key shows the alert without a toast.

row.$comment: Row shape of a publish and of a search reply. `source` is first-class and must name a manifest sources[].name; routing source_id stays host-stamped and never crosses the wire. `confirm` is the question the host asks before it acts on the row (see `confirmation`); the row comes back in its resolve as it was sent, `confirm` included.

lifecycle.$comment: The manifest `lifecycle` key. Absent, the surfaces decide (resident, on-demand, status-bound; see docs/plugin-protocol.md Activation). `publish_then_exit` is a catalog-only plugin: `exec` and pushed `sources` (none declares `live`), none of the surfaces a live child serves (`forbids`). Its run is `on_start`: it publishes its catalog and exits 0 on its own, and the host keeps the catalog, reports the plugin as `published`, counts that exit as success (no restart, no failure budget) and answers its performs `unhandled` (its rows carry host effects). A non-zero exit or a signal is still a crash. The host runs it again when its `[plugins.<id>]` settings change, when a file named by one of its `watch_settings` changes (`watch_settings` lists setting names whose string value is a path: `~` expands to the home, a relative path is under the plugin root; the key needs this lifecycle), on `plugins reload`, and when its own files change. Such a plugin receives no events, the running-apps snapshot included.

source_live.$comment: The manifest sources[].live key. Absent, the source is a pushed catalog (`publish`). `per_query` and `per_scope` make it live: it stays out of the default pool and of the catalog store, and the host pulls it with `search` only while a flashlight query is scoped to it (`@<type>`, or a bang bound to it). per_query is pulled on every change of the query text. per_scope is pulled once per scope with an empty query: its rows are the same whatever is typed, and the host filters them itself. A manifest's sources all declare the same `live`, or none does, and a live source is never `kind: locations` (location rows belong to the default pool). A plugin with live sources and none of pushed sources, query, hints or an observed status is on demand: its first search or perform spawns it, and a search waits out that startup before its own deadline starts. A `listen` beside live sources feeds their rows and keeps no process: the events are delivered from that first search or perform on.

source_types.$comment: Every manifest sources[] entry declares one `type`, the one word users filter the flashlight by (`@tabs`). A type matches `pattern`. `core` types are fed by Flash alone; a plugin declaring one fails to load. A `shared` type fixes the `kind` every source of it declares. Any other matching word is a new type, and every plugin declaring it must agree on its kind. The plugin! macro checks each manifest against this table at build time; the host checks again at load.

hint_target.$comment: The host revalidates geometry and target identity before clicking. context_id is an optional non-empty opaque string identifying the containing live source context; a changed context cancels the captured target. Omitted or null means unspecified.

text_grid_cell.$comment: The exact key set of a text_grid reply's cell, in AppKit points: one cell's width and height (> 0) and the padding between the window's left and top edges and the grid (>= 0). A terminal that centres or pads its grid reports it here; every key is required and a malformed cell rejects the whole reply.

text_grid_line.$comment: The two exact key sets of a text_grid line; rows and columns are cells, row 0 at the top, row < rows and column < columns. text is captured cell text, one UTF-16 unit per cell from column on (a terminal capture's addressing). format is an expanded tmux status format the host lays out across width >= 1 cells (column + width <= columns) with its status-line rules; style markers are not text and a blank layout is dropped. One malformed line rejects the whole reply.

effects.$comment: Closed union. copy_text/insert_text everywhere; open on rows only (answers cannot manufacture navigation). There is deliberately no run effect — argv side effects belong in perform, inside the sandbox.

quotas.$comment: Atomic rejection doctrine: any violation rejects the complete payload (a publish keeps the previous catalog; a reply serves empty); nothing is ever truncated. catalog_rows and catalog_bytes bound the plugin's whole catalog after a per-source merge. catalog_bytes counts the `rows` array as written on the wire — each row object's span in the publish frame, one separator byte per row and the two brackets — measured by the host from the frame it received, never by re-encoding: the compact encoding is the floor, and a plugin pays for whitespace or escaping it adds inside a row (the Rust SDK writes compact rows, so its count is the compact encoding exactly). answers_bytes counts the compact encoding of `answers`. catalog_rows and catalog_bytes bound a `search` reply's rows too, the bytes counted from the compact encoding of `rows`. inline_preview_bytes is the one bound that drops a part, not the payload: it counts the percent-encoded body of a `#[popup=inline:…]` marker in a status segment as written, and a larger body leaves the segment's visible markup without its preview. fetch_response_bytes and fetch_timeout_ms bound a host.fetch response unless the manifest's fetch_limits set others, each at most fetch_response_bytes_max and fetch_timeout_ms_max. alert_title_bytes and alert_value_bytes bound the strings of a perform reply's alert. confirm_bytes bounds a row's `confirm` and a manifest command's.

errors.$comment: Canonical EXACT protocol-level error strings (spec-pinned; domain failures stay free-form and content-free). The response law: every result carries boolean `ok`; ok:false carries a non-empty `error` — except perform's {ok:false, unhandled:true} (not mine; host MAY fall back). A perform {ok:false, error} means mine-but-broke: the host MUST NOT fall back.
errors.protocol_mismatch: protocol version mismatch: host v<H>, plugin v1
errors.initialize_repeated: initialize may only be called once
errors.confirmation_required: requires a perform the user confirmed
errors.user_request_required: requires the user to be using the plugin

id_semantics: positive monotonic integers per sender; host and plugin counters are independent and may overlap (an inbound id+method frame is always a request). Exactly one reply per id'd request. Responses to unknown ids are dropped silently. There is no cancellation: late replies are dropped and the deadline table is the contract.

trace.host_to_plugin: optional `trace` key on a request envelope (hints, text_grid, evaluate, search, perform) naming the user interaction that caused it
trace.plugin_to_host: a `log` notification emitted while serving that request carries it back as params.trace; a malformed id is ignored

deadline.host_to_plugin: optional `deadline_ms` on a request envelope: the milliseconds the host still waits for the reply as it writes the request, a positive integer
deadline.plugin: a hints, text_grid or search handler still running a tenth of the deadline (at most 50 ms) before it is dropped and answers errors.deadline_exceeded; evaluate and perform run to completion

encoding: UTF-8 JSON, one object per newline-terminated line both directions; geometry in NSScreen coordinates; undecodable or oversized lines are dropped (never fatal), the stream self-heals at the next newline; EOF discards an unterminated record before shutdown

transport_limits.$comment: Per-process admission bounds. Plugin replacement-event overflow retains one latest slot per coalescing key (host_events) in addition to the ordinary event backlog, at most plugin_replacement_slots keys at once; each slot obeys frame_bytes, and a new key beyond the bound is dropped like an overflowing ordinary event. A full synchronous control reply queue closes the transport rather than blocking the stdin reader.
